title: Grateful Dead Live at The Scope on 1982-04-03
lineage: Up Front Audience, Sennheiser 441 Microphones > Cassette Master > DAT (via Fostex D-10 Playback) > CD-R (hhb 800 Standalone) > EAC 0.9 > WAV > CDRWAV (for track recutting)>SHN (via MKWACT)

ai_review.summary: High‑energy early‑80s show with scorching Eyes, Scarlet > Fire and a killer second set captured on a surprisingly clear audience tape.
ai_review.review: The Norfolk performance shines thanks to an electrifying second set – standout renditions of Eyes, Scarlet > Fire, Althea, CC Rider into Fire and a soaring Not‑Fade‑Away.  The audience (AUD) recording, taken with Sennheiser mics in the pit, is unusually crisp for a crowd tape though it suffers from an early vocal mic drop and occasional room muddiness.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews rate the show 4‑5 stars and praise its energy and setlist; recording quality is praised as good for an AUD source with only minor flaws.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear up‑front sound with strong instrument separation; occasional mic dropout on Jerry’s vocals early in the first set and some room ambience, but overall a very listenable audience capture.

standout_songs: CC Rider > Fire on the Mountain
poor_songs: Second‑set closing segment (not‑fade ending) noted as less than smoking by a few reviewers
show_quality.setlist_flow: Smooth transitions, especially the CC Rider into Fire and the tight flow of the second set; the first set builds nicely with Althea and Estimated Prophet setting up the high‑energy climax.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for shredding guitar work, quick tempo on Eyes, and a lively interplay with Brent after switching sides.
band_member_comments.Phil: Often lamented that his bass is hard to hear in the AUD source, but many note his powerful playing (“Phil bombs”) when it does come through.
band_member_comments.Bob: Highlighted for ripping rhythm guitar throughout, especially on Scarlet > Fire and the first‑set jams.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent's keyboards receive strong compliments for interstellar interplay with Jerry and for driving the jam sections.
